modules.html:
Wisdom teeth don’t have to be a hassle

Wisdom tooth discomfort often starts small: a little pressure, occasional tenderness, difficulty chewing. But as these third molars push for space, swelling, inflammation, and shifting teeth can follow. While the idea of removal may feel intimidating, the truth is that the procedure is quick, highly predictable, and easier than most people expect.

At My Dear Dentist, your Montrose wisdom tooth removal is performed with gentle techniques, modern technology, and a comfort-first approach. Dr. Nour Amin and Dr. Mustafa Shinta guide you through every step with clear communication and calm, reassuring care.

Schedule your wisdom tooth removal consultation today and find lasting relief.
Key advantages of wisdom teeth extraction

No more food traps

Wisdom teeth create tight, hard-to-clean spaces where food and bacteria get trapped, increasing the risk of cavities and gum inflammation.

Prevent bite issues

As wisdom teeth grow, they can place pressure on surrounding teeth, shifting your bite and causing discomfort or TMJ strain.

Reduce inflammation

Partially erupted wisdom teeth often lead to swollen, tender gums and repeated infections. Removing them stops the cycle.

Improve overall oral health

Eliminating impacted or problematic teeth creates a healthier environment for the rest of your smile.
Your guide to wisdom tooth removal

items.title: How many days does it take to recover?
items.html: Most patients feel significantly better within 2–4 days. Full healing can take a couple of weeks, but your daily routine usually returns to normal quickly.

items.title: How painful is the procedure?
items.html: During the procedure, you won’t feel anything thanks to numbing and sedation options. Afterward, soreness is expected but manageable with medication, rest, and simple home care.

items.title: Is it true that day 3 is the worst after wisdom teeth removal?
items.html: Yes, swelling often peaks around day 3. The good news? That’s when healing starts turning the corner.

items.title: Should I get my wisdom teeth removed?
items.html: You should consider removal if they’re causing pain, crowding, swelling, infections, or are likely to cause issues in the near future. We’ll take digital x-rays to guide you.

items.title: What’s the best aftercare tip?
items.html: Rest, stay hydrated, avoid straws, and skip smoking. Gentle care = smoother healing.
